lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI

steps.title: Install packages and create root endpoint
steps.instructions: In an empty project folder, run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`. Create `main.py`, instantiate `app = FastAPI()`, and define a `@app.get("/")` root route returning a small JSON dict.

targets.caption: Define the root GET decorator and handler in main.py

hints: Start by installing fastapi and uvicorn via pip in your terminal.
Create a file named main.py and import FastAPI from fastapi.
Instantiate app = FastAPI() and decorate def root() with @app.get("/").
common_mistakes: Forgetting to install uvicorn alongside fastapi.
Naming the file something other than main.py without updating the uvicorn command later.
steps.run_command: pip install fastapi && pip install uvicorn
steps.code: from fastapi import FastAPI; app = FastAPI(); @app.get("/") def root(): return {"Hello": "World"}

steps.title: Run the server with Uvicorn
steps.instructions: Start the development server with `uvicorn main:app --reload`. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000` in your browser to see the JSON response.
hints: Run uvicorn with <filename>:<app_variable> and the --reload flag.
The command is uvicorn main:app --reload.
common_mistakes: Running uvicorn in the wrong directory where main.py does not exist.
Forgetting to save main.py before starting the server.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: In main.py, initialize `items = []` and add a `@app.post("/items")` route that appends `item: str` to `items` and returns `items`. With uvicorn running, open a second terminal and POST an item with curl, e.g. `?item=apple`.

targets.caption: Add the POST /items endpoint to append items

hints: Declare an empty list items = [] above your routes.
Use @app.post("/items") with def create_item(item: str): and append item to items.
Send the item via ?item=apple in your curl -X POST URL.
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post for item creation.
Sending a GET request from curl when testing a POST endpoint.
steps.code: items = []; @app.post("/items") def create_item(item: str): items.append(item); return items

steps.title: Add GET endpoint by item ID
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` taking `item_id: int` and returning `items[item_id]`. Re-add items via POST since saving reloads memory, then fetch index 0 with curl GET.

targets.caption: Define the path parameter route for a single item

hints: Include {item_id} inside the @app.get path string.
Accept item_id: int in get_item so FastAPI converts the path string to an integer.
Re-run your POST requests after saving main.py before requesting /items/0.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that --reload clears the in-memory items list on every file save.
Omitting the int type hint on item_id, which causes a TypeError when indexing the list.
steps.code: @app.get("/items/{item_id}") def get_item(item_id: int) -> str: item = items[item_id]; return item

steps.title: Handle missing items with HTTPException
steps.instructions: Import HTTPException from fastapi in main.py and make get_item raise a 404 when item_id >= len(items). Test a missing index like /items/3 with curl.

targets.caption: Raise a 404 HTTPException when item_id is out of bounds

hints: Import HTTPException alongside FastAPI at the top of main.py.
Check if item_id < len(items) before indexing into items.
In the else branch, raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found").
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import HTTPException from fastapi.
Returning HTTPException instead of raising it with the raise keyword.
steps.code: from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException; if item_id < len(items): return items[item_id]; else: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")

steps.title: Add query parameter to list items
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items")` with `def list_items(limit: int = 10):` returning `items[0:limit]`. Test the endpoint with and without `?limit=3` using curl.

targets.caption: Add GET /items with a default limit query parameter

hints: Create a new @app.get("/items") route above get_item.
Give list_items a parameter limit: int = 10.
Return items[0:limit] and test ?limit=3 in curl.
common_mistakes: Wrapping quotes improperly around URLs containing ? in the terminal.
Defining /items/{item_id} without noticing route ordering, though /items is static.

steps.title: Validate request payloads with Pydantic
steps.instructions: In main.py, import `BaseModel` from `pydantic`, define `class Item(BaseModel)` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, and make `create_item` take an `Item`. POST JSON with curl (e.g. `-d '{"text":"apple"}'`) and confirm a payload missing `text` fails validation.

targets.caption: Define the Pydantic model and use it in create_item
The POST response echoes the validated item

hints: Import BaseModel from pydantic and subclass it as class Item(BaseModel):.
Remove = None from text: str to make text a required field.
Send the item as a JSON body with curl -d '{"text":"apple"}' instead of a query parameter.
common_mistakes: Still passing ?item=apple in the URL query string after switching create_item to Item.
Leaving text: str = None when trying to enforce required field validation.
steps.code: from pydantic import BaseModel; class Item(BaseModel): text: str; is_done: bool = False; def create_item(item: Item): items.append(item); return items

steps.title: Add response models to GET endpoints
steps.instructions: Add `response_model=list[Item]` to the GET /items decorator and `response_model=Item` to GET /items/{item_id} in main.py.

targets.caption: Specify response_model on your GET decorators

hints: Pass response_model= as a keyword argument inside @app.get(...).
Use list[Item] for list_items and Item for get_item.
common_mistakes: Putting response_model inside the function signature instead of the @app.get decorator.
Using Item instead of list[Item] on the list_items endpoint.
steps.code: @app.get("/items", response_model=list[Item]); @app.get("/items/{item_id}", response_model=Item); def get_item(item_id: int) -> Item:

steps.title: Test endpoints in interactive docs
steps.instructions: With uvicorn running, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, expand POST /items, click Try it out, submit a JSON item and click Execute. Also look at /redoc and /openapi.json.

targets.caption: Use Swagger UI at /docs to execute API requests
Send the request and inspect the response body

hints: Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in your web browser.
Expand the POST /items section and click the Try it out button.
Edit the JSON request body and click Execute to inspect the response.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the /docs path suffix when opening the local server URL.
Providing invalid JSON syntax (such as trailing commas) in the Swagger UI request body.
